# Pandamonium v1.0.63

This patch train ships three reviewed changes: the Add Plugins modal is now tabbed with dedicated navigation for installed plugin details and a URL-only GitHub intake, the composer gains a session identity selector with the identity's default model chip and a real reasoning-level display, and the active workspace becomes settable from the picker and by the agent with honest errors. CT103 updates through the signed updater with rollback to v1.0.62.

## MAD-883 — Workspace: make active workspace settable and visible to the agent

### Problem

The operator reported there was no way to set the active workspace to work out of. The picker and slash command existed, but failures looked like an absent feature, the setting lived only in one browser's local storage, and the in-app agent had no way to set, clear, or report the workspace.

### Implementation

Commits `a50984da` and `03bb21b2` (PR #214, merge `3eba6956`): the active workspace persists per chat session and the picker surfaces honest errors instead of a generic browse failure, and a new `manage_workspace` tool lets the agent set, clear, and report the active workspace with server validation through the existing confinement path. Commit `8c970dc6` makes the picker spec deterministic in CI.

### Product value and UI visibility

The workspace pill, overflow picker, and `/workspace set` now agree on the per-session active workspace, and agents can change it when asked. Errors tell the operator what actually failed (authentication, missing folder, or unsupported path) rather than implying the feature is missing.

### Verification

The focused picker, workspace, and agent-tool checks pass, the deterministic browser spec is stable in CI, and PR #214 checks are green. The v1.0.63 release candidate runs the full Python and Chromium suites.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No dependency or database change; the workspace confinement semantics (`vet_workspace` and path resolvers) are unchanged. Workspace state remains per chat session, and unauthenticated or non-admin sessions still cannot browse host folders by design.

## MAD-930 — Composer: identity selector, identity-default model chip, and real reasoning level

### Problem

The composer's left chip showed the identity name but could not switch it, there was no visible link between an identity and the model it loads, and the reasoning chip said "Default" instead of the level the selected model is actually set to.

### Implementation

Commits `4c82c5c3`, `6023603f`, and `f7ec7913` (PR #218, merge `707e35fc`): the identity chip becomes a session identity selector, a new chip to its right loads and overrides the selected identity's attached default model for the session without mutating the saved identity profile, and the reasoning chip resolves the real level from the existing reasoning-level path instead of the literal "Default".

### Product value and UI visibility

Switching identity immediately updates the model chip to that identity's default and the reasoning chip to the real level; overriding the model in the composer applies to the current session only. The capability-aware footer and keyboard/mobile behavior from the existing selector are preserved.

### Verification

The new composer source and browser checks cover identity switching, per-session model override, and the reasoning label, and the existing selector acceptance specs still pass. PR #218 checks are green; the v1.0.63 release candidate runs the full Python and Chromium suites.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Composer display and session routing only: no provider or endpoint contract changes, no new dependencies. Saved identity profiles are not modified by a session override.

### References

## MAD-946 — Plugins: split Add Plugins into Installed and Add tabs with dedicated plugin-detail navigation

### Problem

The Add Plugins modal stacked search, Add from GitHub, the scan panel, the installed list, and plugin details into one surface. Clicking an installed plugin opened a side-by-side detail column, and the Add-from-GitHub form still asked for a ref (`HEAD`) that the operator never wants to type.

### Implementation

Commit `95c47c3e` (PR #220, merge `dba7e956`): the modal is split into **Installed plugins** (default) and **Add a new plugin** tabs. The installed list is full width and a click opens the plugin details as their own view with a persistent "← Back to installed" button; no side-by-side column remains. The Add tab keeps marketplace browse (search, categories, refresh, catalog list and detail) and a URL-only GitHub intake — the ref input is removed, scans resolve the default-branch HEAD, and installs still pin the scanned revision. The idle scan card no longer leaks through the `hidden` attribute.

### Product value and UI visibility

Installed plugins are the first thing the operator sees, and details are reachable without sharing the screen; adding a plugin is one pasted URL and a scan. Tab switching is keyboard reachable (arrow keys and standard tab semantics), and the mobile layout keeps the dedicated back navigation.

### Verification

Twenty-two focused Chromium specs pass across the marketplace, installed, intake, wizard empty-state, dock-freeze, and modal-lifecycle suites, asserting tab switching, the installed detail/back navigation, the absent ref input, and the approval flow inside the Add tab. The full Chromium suite passed 150/150, and PR #220 checks are green.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

UI layout and navigation only: no API, registry, scanner, installer, or authority change, and no new dependencies. Approval previews, scan progress, and installed-detail content are unchanged as information.
